title: Reserved inference seller brief
content:
Purpose:
This is a seller-focused, procurement-ready brief for Redwood Dedicated (reserved inference capacity). Target is commercial AEs and solutions engineers working on mid-market and enterprise deals where predictable throughput, strong isolation, and contractual SLAs are the primary purchase triggers.

A quick note on voice: this is a working draft — mix of crisp messaging and tactical talking points you can use in calls, procurement cycles, and SOWs. Add anecdotes from live deals (Slack thread: #closed-deals-dedicated) and push updates into the canonical Confluence page.

Buyer personas in focus:
- Platform/Infrastructure Lead (Platform team): cares about isolation, network controls, and predictable tail latency for customer-facing features.
- ML/Inference Lead (ML Eng): cares about throughput (tokens/sec), model compatibility, KV cache persistence, and model version pinning.
- Procurement / Finance: cares about predictable unit economics, contractual SLAs, auditability, and billing cadence.
- Security/Compliance: cares about VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and data residency.

Top-level value prop (single-sentence):
Reserved inference capacity from Redwood gives your engineering org predictable throughput, contractual SLAs, and strict data isolation so product teams can ship latency-sensitive LLM features without surprise costs or reliability regressions.

Core messages to prioritize (by buyer):
- Platform / ML: "Deterministic throughput — reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling policies and dedicated KV cache backing means you get sustained tokens/sec guarantees and stable P99 latency as your traffic grows."
- Procurement / Finance: "Fixed committed capacity with consumption smoothing and transparent unit economics — fewer billing surprises and clear cost per 1M tokens at your committed tier."
- Security: "Private control plane options, VPC peering, and KMS integrations give you audit trails and key isolation for regulated workloads."

Competitive positioning (short bullets):
- Versus hyperscalers with managed endpoints: Hyperscalers offer scale but often add unpredictable throttling/surge behavior and tangled networking constraints. Redwood Dedicated is opinionated for inference and provides predictable per-commit throughput and optimizations (batching, KV cache) tuned to LLM patterns.
- Versus inference-only runtimes (self-hosted): Self-hosted gives control but leaves customers to build observability, rollout tools, and SRE runbooks. We bundle runtime ops, rollouts, and SLO-driven fallbacks so customers avoid a months-long operational burden.
- Versus other LLM API vendors: Our differentiator is the unified interface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — same API, same rollout primitives, and the ability to scale from self-serve to reserved contracted capacity.

Common procurement objections and scripts
1) "We already have GPUs in house"
   - Script: "Totally reasonable — many customers use Redwood Dedicated alongside their infra. We can operate in a hybrid model or run a 90-day trial on a small reserved pool so you compare unit economics for production traffic. Also consider SRE maintenance time saved vs. capex ops."
2) "We need strong SLAs before committing"
   - Script: "Our standard Dedicated SLA covers availability and tail latency objectives for provisioned pools; we also offer escalated enterprise SLAs with dedicated on-call during onboarding. I can share the SLA appendix and a short checklist your legal team can use to speed review."
3) "How is data isolated?"
   - Script: "Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated at the GPU and network level, control plane can be private (VPC) and we support KMS-backed keying and audit logs. We can list the controls for your security questionnaire."

Procurement checklist (what to include in proposals / SOWs)
- Capacity definition: GPU type(s), quantity, guaranteed concurrent sessions, expected tokens/sec baseline, and burst buffer policy.
- SLA metrics: availability (monthly uptime %), P95/P99 latency targets for a defined token size distribution, and credit/remedy clauses.
- Isolation & security: VPC peering, private control plane, key management, and SOC/ISO compliance attestations.
- Operational playbook: maintenance windows, planned scale events, rollback/fallback model variants and notifications.
- Cost & billing: committed monthly/annual spend, overage pricing, refund/credit mechanics, and invoice cadence.
- Onboarding milestones: test traffic, golden prompt suite, throughput validation, and canary rollout plan.

SLA language (seller-friendly snippet to include in initial SOWs)
"Redwood shall ensure the provisioned Dedicated Pool achieves: 99.9% monthly availability for the pool, and P99 inference latency not to exceed 250ms for requests with <=1024 tokens under baseline load as defined in Appendix A. In the event of failure to meet these targets, Customer will be eligible for service credits as specified in Section X."
(Notes: exact numbers are negotiable per customer tier. Use 99.95% and 200–300ms P99 for enterprise tiers with dedicated on-call.)

Throughput guarantees — how to present them empirically
- Baseline: "Committed GPU pool = sustained X tokens/sec for a 1024-token median request size with concurrency Y."
- Burst: "Burst capacity allowed up to Z% above baseline for up to N minutes per hour, subject to autoscaling policy."
- Observability: Include a sample dashboard snapshot (link to confluence) that maps tokens/sec, avg token cost, P95/P99 latency. Buyers prefer a simple chart that maps committed GPUs -> steady-state tokens/sec.

ROI/Value math (short example to hand to procurement)
- Customer estimate: 10M tokens/day production, 10% traffic growth, 30% improvement in ops overhead from moving off self-hosted.
- Simple comparison: cost_per_1M_tokens_reserved vs cost_per_1M_tokens_on_demand + internal_ops_hours.
- Offer: 12-month commit with quarterly throughput verification; include a break clause at 210 days with scaled refund if Redwood misses agreed onboarding milestones.

Negotiation playbook (what AEs can concede vs. escalate)
- Concede quickly: small onboarding credits, pilot period with limited refunds, 30–60 day grace on scale changes.
- Escalate: changes to baseline SLA numbers (availability %, P99 target), permanent price discounts below standard committed tiers, or changes to core isolation guarantees.

Sales enablement assets to attach (ask product/comm to update if stale)
- One-pager: "How reserved capacity maps to tokens/sec" (must include GPU mapping table).
- Demo kit: scripted canary test showing 5–10k concurrent short chat sessions with P99 latency plot.
- Procurement cheat sheet: sample SOW clauses, security questionnaire answers, and a one-page SLA appendix.

Email template excerpt (for procurement outreach)
Hi [Procurement Lead],

Following our conversation, attaching the proposed reserved capacity terms we discussed. Key points: dedicated GPU pools, private control plane option, and SLA for monthly availability and P99 latency. Happy to schedule a 30-minute legal/ops walkthrough to expedite review.

Next steps / TODOs (owner):
- Validate current SLA appendix with Legal (Marcus Lee) — due 2026-03-17.
- Update the GPU->tokens/sec mapping table with latest benchmarks from Serving Runtime (ask Applied ML for numbers) — Priya Raman.
- Create a simplified procurement one-pager and add to partner folder — Diego Alvarez.
- Run 2 buyer-scenario roleplays with AE team this week and collect the top 6 objections.

Appendix / quick notes:
- Typical enterprise ask: pin model version + pinned KV cache snapshot for reproducible outputs — this is an advanced feature we can include for +$X/month.
- Fallback policy: default rollout is canary -> linear -> global; for Dedicated we can configure automatic fallback to smaller compatible model variant if pool is overloaded.
- Legal: standard dedicated SOW includes data processing addendum and SOC2 attestation; some customers ask for contract redlines around indemnity which need Legal review.

Hand-off: Use this brief as the canonical seller checklist for outbound deals targeting reserved commitments. Add field notes after each closed/lost deal as "postmortem-bid-XXXXX" in the shared drive.
